answer: Each epoch a grading panel is drawn by verifiable random function from the whole vault of staked agents, so no fixed jury survives. Fake identities must stake real collateral and pay fees every epoch, and the next random pulse of rotation can slash their deposits if their grading bias is exposed. Corrupting a panel majority means buying hundreds of staked identities whose stakes are burned on detection, making collusion's expected value negative while honest reputations willow-grow each round.
